agree.reason: Opening with the late report and a named accountable person speaks to Marisol's main worry, and the figures make a clear case, but she may still hesitate over running costs once reserves fall to $11,000.

honest.reason: It drops the brief's unsupported 'double' claim in favour of a figure the facts support (half again for the summer, 81,000 against 72,000 for the year), though the closing 'those 9,000 pounds will reach' reads as more certain than repeat farm offers allow, and the board-member and six-month reporting commitments are new promises that aren't in the brief.

works_the_facts.reason: The derived figures are correct and well chosen: 18,000 to 27,000 pounds for the summer, about 15 pounds per household (9,000 ÷ 610), 72,000 to 81,000 pounds a year, 'more than a quarter' of the cost, and 'nearly two-thirds' of the $29,000 reserves.

right_comparison.reason: It states the alternative plainly: without the van, farm offers are turned down again and fresh food stays at 6,000 pounds a month. It gives no trend, but the brief offers none.

qualification.reason: The goal has a number (9,000 pounds) and check points (reports at six and twelve months), but the only consequence of missing it is an explanation, and the goal assumes farms make similar offers without saying so.

objections.reason: It meets the late-report objection directly and covers driver reliability, but it doesn't address fuel, insurance and maintenance against an $11,000 reserve, or cold storage once the food arrives, which the brief names as part of the original problem.

fit.reason: It's a clearly sectioned grant narrative just under the 500-word limit.
